To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for packing fat objects that uses linear space and has running time O((log n)(d+1)(log log n)(d+3)), and (2) there is a PTAS for piercing fat objects that uses polynomial space and has running-time O(n(log n)(d+2)(log log n)^{d+3})
(1) there is an efficient algorithm for packing fat objects that uses only linear space, and (2), there is an efficient linear-space algorithm for piercing fat objects.

(a) we describe a shifted hierarchical subdivision algorithm for packing with a time bound of O(1) ^{d} n log ^{d+1} n, (b) we describe a geometric separators algorithm for packing and piercing with a time bound O(1) n log ^{d} n, and (c) the latter algorithm uses only O(n) space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two questions: (i) Can the time bound of the shifted hierarchical subdivision method be further improved? (ii) Can the space bound be improved to linear?
developing efficient approximation schemes for packing/piercing fat objects.
two questions: How much time and space is required to solve the packing and piercing problems for fat objects?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problems of packing and piercing fat sets are solvable in polynomial time, and that these algorithms run in time O(n log^d n) and O(n^d log n).

we have developed a new PTAS for packing fat objects that has better running time than Erlebach et~al.'s, uses only linear space instead of polynomial space, and can be applied to piercing fat objects, for which no polynomial-time approximation scheme was known before.

the shifted hierarchical subdivision method can also be applied successfully to problems in fixed dimensions.
